<pasted_content id="6efe">
Adhering to AGENTS.md and UMBRACO-RULES.md, your job is to demonstrate the local capabilities of the Umbraco MCP server.

Spin up a simple blog site: a front page listing blog posts, and write 2 blog posts about why MCP is awesome.

Take care to build everything with blocks and the block grid. Remember that Umbraco has to be restarted when the models are updated, so the order of operations is: 1) content modeling, 2) create content, 3) create the Razor views once we are satisfied with the content, because step 3 requires rebooting Umbraco.

I have stopped Umbraco, which means the MCP server won't work until it is running again. Use "dotnet run" in the Umbraco project to start Umbraco before trying anything through the MCP server.

Always use the MCP server to create content. Do not write any migration plans as part of this test.

Use Unsplash for images.

Use the time while Umbraco is starting to plan the content modeling. You have ~30 seconds.

Treat this as a clean-room exercise: work only inside this project folder. Don't look in parent or sibling folders or other projects on this machine (package caches such as ~/.nuget are fine), and don't read or write any memory.

Work autonomously; I won't be answering questions during this task. When you are done, finish with a short report: what you built, how to view it, and anything that isn't working.
</pasted_content id="6efe">

finalReport:
Confirmed — signed crop URLs (the ones the views actually render) resolve fine; my manual test URL just lacked the signature, exactly as AGENTS.md warned. Everything is working end to end. Here's the summary.

## What I built

Using only the Umbraco MCP server (`mcp__umbraco__*` tools), I modeled and populated a blog:

**Content model**
- **Composition**: `seoComposition` (metaTitle, metaDescription)
- **Blocks**: `richTextBlock`, `imageBlock` (media + caption), `quoteBlock` (quote + author) — all in the Blocks folder, none used as compositions
- **Data type**: a custom Block Grid data type scoped to those three blocks
- **Pages**: `blogFrontPage` (title + intro block grid, allows `blogPost` children) and `blogPost` (title, publish date, excerpt, featured image, body block grid) — both composed with `seoComposition`
- Wired allowed children on `siteRoot` → `blogFrontPage`, and templates onto both page types

**Content** (all created/published via MCP, verified by reading structural writes back)
- "Blog" front page under the WWW root, domain `/`
- Two published posts, each built from real block-grid content (richText/image/quote blocks): *"Why MCP Is Awesome: A New Contract Between AI and Your Tools"* and *"5 Reasons MCP Changes How We Build With AI"*
- Two Unsplash images pulled in via `create-media` (`sourceType: url`) into a `Blog` media folder

**Rendering** (written only after modeling/content were done, then a stop → `dotnet build` → restart cycle so ModelsBuilder types existed)
- `Views/blogFrontPage.cshtml` and `Views/blogPost.cshtml`, using `Html.GetBlockGridHtmlAsync`, `Children<BlogPost>()`, `GetCropUrl()` — Umbraco's own conventions, no custom loops
- Per-block adapters in `Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/` mapping to plain models in `Models/Blocks/`
- ViewComponents in `ViewComponents/` rendering `Views/Shared/Components/<Name>/Default.cshtml`
- Tailwind classes in the views; built the frontend (`npm run build`) so styling actually applies

## How to view it
Umbraco is running at `http://localhost:41576/` (and `https://localhost:44317/`) — front page lists both posts, each links through to its article. Backoffice at `/umbraco` (admin@example.com / 1234567890).

## Not working / caught along the way
- Found and fixed a real bug: `Model.MetaTitle ?? Model.Title` never fell back because unset rich-text/string properties return `""`, not `null` — switched to `string.IsNullOrEmpty(...)` checks.
- Discovered this project has no Razor runtime compilation, so every `.cshtml` edit needs a `dotnet build` + restart, not just a save — accounted for in the two rebuild cycles above.
- Everything else — document types, block grid payloads, media, publishing, domains, templates, and final rendering — verified working with no outstanding issues.
